criteria: Exclude paraphrases that ask for the same decision or rule. Also consolidate narrower questions when a retained question explicitly tests all their required facts, including single/multiple-answer and case variants. Keep related questions when a different product configuration, operation, rule, permission or material constraint changes the required decision. Similarity scores produce review candidates only; never merge automatically.

groups.reason: Both identify the Container Apps environment as the VNet boundary shared by all its apps. The environment question already identifies its Log Analytics workspace. The separate destination question repeats that same configuration fact; naming console/system logs does not change the destination.
Both require multiple-revision mode and percentage traffic weights for a canary release.
Both ask which identity lets a Container App pull from a private ACR: managed identity with AcrPull.
Both choose Session consistency for read-your-own-writes without Strong consistency's cost; the catalogue case does not change the decision.
Both use WaitForExternalEvent for a multi-day human approval, with dehydration while waiting and an optional durable timeout. Retain the more explicit two-answer version.
Both require a transactional outbox and relay to coordinate an external database write with message publication. The order case adds no different transaction constraint.
Both require Service Bus sessions to preserve FIFO processing for related messages sharing a SessionId; the customer case repeats this rule.

Both preserve per-device ordering by using the device or vehicle ID as the Event Hubs partition key. The per-device item requires events to share a partition to preserve ordering. The standalone within-partition ordering item repeats that underlying guarantee; retain the applied partition-key question.
Both test the same bound: parallel consumers in one consumer group are limited by partition count. Eight consumers is only a numeric example.
Both buffer notifications in a queue and throttle its consumer to protect a downstream API limited to ten requests per second.
Both grant secret-value reads without management permissions through the Key Vault Secrets User role.
Both limit compromise blast radius with separate vaults per application/environment and narrowly scoped identity permissions.
Both require soft delete and purge protection before using a Key Vault key as a customer-managed key.
Both prevent rotation outages with overlapping credential sets and client-cache refresh on the rotation event. Retain the explicit two-answer case.

Both contrast cheap, fast pre-aggregated metric alerts with more expressive but slower scheduled KQL log alerts. The alert comparison already explicitly identifies scheduled KQL evaluation as a log search alert. The standalone alert-type question repeats that fact without a new alert condition or query.
Both choose sampling to reduce ingestion cost while preserving continuous representative telemetry instead of daily-cap gaps.
Both ask for Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus to collect AKS metrics without operating a Prometheus server, despite appearing in different domains.
Both authenticate CI/CD to Azure without a stored secret by federating the CI provider's identity to an Entra application; pushing to ACR does not change that flow.
Both address a cache stampede when a hot key expires by locking while one caller repopulates it. Keep the fuller question, which also tests TTL jitter.
The two-answer item includes the complete at-least-once/idempotent-handler fact tested by the delivery-guarantee item, and additionally tests dead-letter preservation.
The comprehensive item tests both automatic dead-letter conditions. The before-first-delivery variant narrows the answer to its TTL-expiry condition without adding a new configuration rule.

The billing case explicitly requires both publisher duplicate detection and consumer idempotency using processed MessageIds. The individual questions repeat those same controls; keep the combined case.

The two-answer item explicitly tests additive/inherited allow permissions and deny precedence. The Reader/Contributor example and the deny-mechanism question repeat those rules without adding a new scope or evaluation rule.
The tracing case explicitly requires cloud_RoleName for service attribution and operation_Id for request correlation. The individual field questions repeat exactly these two facts.

The two-probe item already requires readiness to stop routing traffic to an unhealthy pod. The rolling-update/502 variant repeats that readiness role, while the retained item also tests startup behavior.

The case already explicitly requires mounting Key Vault secrets with the Secrets Store CSI Driver. The standalone mounted-files question adds no different delivery mechanism; the case additionally tests workload identity.
Both give independent consumers separate consumer groups so each reads the stream. The case includes that exact decision and also tests replay retention.

retainedExamples.reason: Redis and PostgreSQL require different service-specific authentication configuration; PostgreSQL also requires supplying the Entra token as the protocol password.
The consumer-parallelism bound and the inability to reduce a deployed partition count are different operational rules.
Diagnosing registry connectivity, designing a private registry and connecting privately to Key Vault have different service targets and configuration constraints.
Tenant-scoped query routing and evenly distributed product access require different partition keys.
Service Bus queue and HTTP scaling require different trigger rules, even though both can scale to zero.
Diagnosing an existing HNSW index that is not used differs from choosing both an index and a compatible operator for an unindexed slow query.
Customer-managed-key prerequisites, deleted-secret recovery and the effect of purge protection test different rules even though they name the same settings.
Naming the automatic Standard-tier scaling setting differs from diagnosing throughput-unit capacity from throttling metrics.
An AKS storage class and a Container Apps environment storage mount require different platform configuration, even though both use Azure Files.
Diagnosing secret-reference authorization can require Get access under an access policy; choosing a least-privilege RBAC data role is a different configuration decision.
Tuning a query-time HNSW search parameter differs from designing indexes for tenant-filtered similarity queries.
Correcting a Pending pod can involve lowering its resource request. Identifying the node autoscaler and designing Spot versus regular node pools test additional operational decisions.
Native delivery destinations that skip validation are different from the source service producing blob lifecycle events.
Stampede prevention using TTL jitter and locking is different from the command that reads a remaining expiry.

expandedReview.reason: Additional answer-subset and same-concept checks after a repeated Key Vault customer-managed-key question was reported. That exact variant was already excluded from new exams; old saved attempts could still contain it.
